summary: Letcher County site known from a May 1931 newspaper report of a planned 50-foot steel tower; Forest Lookouts marks it removed. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: planned fifty-foot steel lookout tower (1931 report; no confirmation that it was built)
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists the tower as removed, with no date.

events.note: Local chief fire warden Chap King said a fifty-foot steel lookout tower would be erected near a state highway within a month or so, with a watchman in fire season. The item looks ahead; it does not report a finished tower.

evidence.supports: 1931 report of a planned fifty-foot steel tower near a state highway
evidence.quote: a fifty foot steel lookout tower will be erected on a high point in the neighborhood of where the State Highway passes over it

evidence.supports: planned watchman during the fire season
evidence.quote: a watchman will occupy the tower, during the dangerous forest fire season

evidence.supports: Chap King was the local chief fire warden
evidence.quote: Chap King. local chief fire warden

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts lists the tower as removed
agency listed as Jefferson National Forest
Jefferson National Forest lands reach into Letcher and Pike counties, Kentucky
evidence.quote: Jefferson National Forest lands stretch from Rockbridge County, Virginia, west into Letcher and Pike counties, Kentucky

notes_for_editor: Only tower-specific source is the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes a May 21, 1931 Mountain Eagle report of a planned tower; no source confirms it was built. Agency claim rests on that page; the WV Encyclopedia supports Jefferson NF land in Letcher and Pike counties but not this site. Two WebSearch calls and NHLR/FFLOS index checks found nothing further. Story about 160 words.
